etymology: Latin: argumentum ad ignorantiam - the absence of proof is offered as proof.
committed_when: Nobody has produced evidence either way.
tell: The conclusion rests on what has not been found.
counter: Ask who holds the burden. A claim still needs support; an absence of evidence is evidence only when the evidence would be expected.
senses: Treating a claim as true because it has not been proven false, or false because it has not been proven true.

It works because the burden of proof feels like a formality. Most audiences assume a claim is either established or refuted, and the sentence supplies the third option, absence, as if it settled the matter.
example: “Nobody has proven the machines are safe.” Nobody has proven them unsafe either; the sentence treats the missing study as a finding.

confused_with.tell: Both outsource the support; ignorance to a gap, authority to a person.
